title: Plan: Date/Time module (swedate.c)
description:
Port swedate.c (~588 lines) to Rust. All pure functions, no global state.

## Functions to port

| C function | Purpose | Complexity |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `swe_julday(year,month,day,hour,gregflag)` | Calendar → Julian Day | Medium — Gregorian/Julian split, sign handling |
| `swe_revjul(jd,gregflag,*year,*month,*day,*hour)` | Julian Day → calendar | Medium — inverse of julday |
| `swe_date_conversion(y,m,d,utime,c,*tjd)` | Validated calendar → JD | Simple — julday + validation |
| `swe_utc_to_jd(iyear,...,dsec,gregflag,*dret,*serr)` | UTC → JD (TT and UT1) | Complex — leap second table, pre/post-1972 handling |
| `swe_jdet_to_utc(tjd_et,gregflag,*iyear,...,*dsec)` | TT JD → UTC calendar | Medium — inverse with leap seconds |
| `swe_jdut1_to_utc(tjd_ut,gregflag,*iyear,...,*dsec)` | UT1 JD → UTC calendar | Medium |
| `swe_utc_time_zone(...)` | Apply timezone offset | Simple — arithmetic with day-boundary crossing |
| `swe_day_of_week(jd)` | Day of week (0=Mon) | Trivial |

## Key algorithm details (from catalogue-internal §7.1)

**Julian Day formula:**
```
u = year; if month < 3: u -= 1
u0 = u + 4712
u1 = month + 1; if u1 < 4: u1 += 12
JD = floor(u0 × 365.25) + floor(30.6 × u1 + 0.000001) + day + hour/24 − 63.5
if Gregorian: u2 = floor(|u|/100) − floor(|u|/400); JD -= u2 + 2
```

**Leap second table:** Static table of 27 dates (1972–2016) plus optional extension from `seleapsec.txt`. Before 1972: input treated as UT1. From 1972: TT = UTC + accumulated_leap_seconds + 32.184s.

## Rust design notes
- Return `Result<JulianDay, Error>` from validated functions, plain `f64` from `julday`/`revjul` (which always succeed)
- Consider a `JulianDay` newtype for type safety (but keep it ergonomic — `Deref<Target=f64>` or just methods)
- Leap second table as a `const` array; loading from file can be a method on `Ephemeris`
- `utc_to_jd` returns a struct `{ tt: f64, ut1: f64 }` instead of C's `dret[2]` array

## Testing
- C test suite: setest/suite_05_date_time.c
- Generate golden data: known dates (J2000=2451545.0, Unix epoch, historical dates, negative years)
- Edge cases: Feb 29 in leap/non-leap years, Julian/Gregorian transition (Oct 1582), leap second dates

## C source reference
- swedate.c:1-588 — all functions above
- swedate.c:159 — julday algorithm
- swedate.c:273 — leap second table

## Dependencies
- Phase 0 (types, constants)

acceptance_criteria.text: julday produces identical results to C swe_julday for Gregorian and Julian calendars, including negative years (BCE) and the Oct 1582 boundary
revjul round-trips with julday for all test inputs
date_conversion rejects invalid dates (Feb 30, month 13) with Error::InvalidDate — proleptic Gregorian is used (no historical gap check), matching C behavior
day_of_week matches C swe_day_of_week for known dates
utc_time_zone handles day boundary crossings and preserves leap seconds (dsec >= 60)
utc_to_jd returns correct (JdTt, JdUt1) for post-1972 dates counting leap seconds from const table
utc_to_jd pre-1972 fast path treats input as UT1 and derives TT via delta-T
utc_to_jd rejects leap second 60 on dates not in the leap second table
jdet_to_utc / jdut1_to_utc correctly detect and output second=60.x during leap second windows
All UTC functions accept &impl DeltaT — no global state, no mutable cache
JdTt and JdUt1 are distinct newtypes that prevent accidental mixing at compile time
Leap second table is a const array; EphemerisConfig accepts optional extra entries and seleapsec.txt path

decisions.decision: Distinct JD newtypes: JdTt(f64) and JdUt1(f64) instead of single JulianDay
decisions.rationale: Prevents the most common class of astronomical bugs — mixing TT and UT1 time scales. Compile-time enforcement. Minimal ergonomics cost with arithmetic trait impls.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Single JulianDay newtype — simpler but allows silent time-scale confusion

decisions.decision: DeltaT trait boundary: date functions accept &impl DeltaT rather than computing internally
decisions.rationale: Keeps date module self-contained and testable without implementing swephlib.c delta-T. Clean dependency inversion. Ephemeris implements the trait later.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Methods on &Ephemeris — would couple date module to Ephemeris and require delta-T implementation upfront

decisions.decision: Free functions with explicit parameters, not methods on Ephemeris
decisions.rationale: Maximally testable, respects stateless invariant. Ephemeris provides thin convenience wrappers.
decisions.rejected_alternative: All functions as methods on &Ephemeris — tighter coupling, harder to unit test

decisions.decision: Leap seconds as hardcoded const [i32; 27] + optional Vec<i32> extension from config
decisions.rationale: Matches C structure. No mutable state. File-loaded extensions stored read-only in Ephemeris at construction time.
decisions.rejected_alternative: LazyLock / OnceLock init — introduces hidden mutable state, violates architecture invariant

decisions.decision: UtcComponents struct for UTC function I/O instead of flat parameter lists
decisions.rationale: 6 parameters is unwieldy. Struct is clear, named, and serves as both input and output type for UTC functions.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Flat args matching C signatures — more error-prone, less idiomatic Rust

execution_record: Divergence from plan: acceptance criterion about Gregorian gap (Oct 5-14 1582) rejection was incorrect. The C library uses proleptic Gregorian calendar — julday/revjul round-trip succeeds for dates in the 'gap', so date_conversion accepts them. Updated criterion to match C behavior.\n\nThree test tolerance fixes: revjul hour round-trip and utc_to_jd TT-UT1 difference assertions were too tight (1e-10 / 1e-12) given floating-point cancellation when adding small delta-T values to large JD numbers. Relaxed to 1e-8 / 1e-9 respectively — still sub-microsecond precision."

messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (35077e3^..35077e3):

Verdict: needs-attention

- [high] stale-table-bypass: utc_to_jd Phase 6 (stale-table fallback, date.rs:219-228) runs before Phase 7 (leap-second validation). A DeltaT provider returning a large enough value (e.g. 75.184/86400 days for 2020) triggers the early-return UT1 fallback, bypassing the leap_secs.contains(&ndat) check entirely. This means utc.second >= 60.0 on a non-leap-second date can return Ok instead of Err(InvalidLeapSecond) — validation correctness depends on the delta-T value rather than the UTC input alone.

Recommendation: Move the leap-second-60 validation (current Phase 7) before the stale-table fallback (current Phase 6), or explicitly reject second >= 60.0 when taking the UT1 fallback path.

No other findings. Risk score 0.292, no constraint/convention violations (sutra_review).
